title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes titled 'Chirurgie des surfaces conformes'. Grothendieck lists elementary surgery operations on a conformal (Riemann) surface X, possibly with boundary, carrying a compact rectifiable 1-complex K. On the previous page: (1) cutting X along K gives a compact bordered surface X~ with distinguished boundary ∂'X~. (2) Regluing X~ along an admissible (rectifiable) equivalence relation on ∂'X~ recovers a conformal surface. (3) Shrinking (rétrécissement): remove a collar annulus of modulus ε_i, with 0 ≤ ε_i < ∞, along each component of ∂'X~ to get X~*. Then choose a rectifiable identification ∂'X~* ≅ ∂'X~ compatible with components, transport the gluing relation, and reglue to get a new pair K ⊂ X*.

This page:
- (4) Elongation is the inverse operation: glue on a collar annulus instead of removing one.
- (5) Mixed operation, 'panachage': take a standard collar neighbourhood T_i of each component (∂'X~)_i. Inside it, take a Jordan curve Γ_i, drawn wavy and not concentric, together with a rectifiable isomorphism Γ_i ≅ (∂'X~)_i. Define X~* by cutting off the part K_i of T_i bounded by Γ_i. The figure, with hatching outside the surface, suggests that Γ_i may run partly inside X~ and partly in an added collar. One then finishes as in 3) and 4) to get X* and K ⊂ X*. The margin notes that such an operation is a composite: shrinking ∘ elongation, or two elongations.
- A second item numbered '4)' states the commutation of the panachage operations attached to different connected components of K.
- (6) For an isolated component C of K that is a real-analytically embedded curve, panachage always decomposes into: 1°) real-analytic removal of an annulus around C; 2°) real-analytic regluing of the two boundary circles of the removed annulus by a cylinder. The sketched cylinders carry wavy transversal curves.
- The page ends with 'relations with the small conformal embeddings of a small annulus'. That is, the local deformation space is governed by germs of conformal embeddings of thin annuli.

In modern terms, this is a toolkit for deforming conformal structures near a graph or curve on a surface. It amounts to cut-and-reglue with modulus changes, as in plumbing, grafting and conformal welding. The deformations relate to Fenchel–Nielsen-type twist and stretch moves and to Schiffer-type variations. The purpose, per the next page, is to study moduli of triples S ⊂ K ⊂ X: Grothendieck's 'cartes' (dessins) with their canonical conformal structures, rigidified by topological types. This links to the Teichmüller-tower and dessins programme of the Esquisse.
errors: Numbering is inconsistent: '4)' is used twice. The commutation item should be 5bis or 6, and 'comme dans 3°), 4°)' presumably refers to shrinking/elongation.

Gap: 'admissible au sens rectifiable' regluing does not by itself guarantee existence of a conformal structure on the glued surface. Removability of rectifiable seams (sets of σ-finite length are conformally removable) gives uniqueness. Existence along an arbitrary rectifiable identification is a conformal welding problem: it needs something like quasisymmetry of the induced boundary homeomorphism in conformal coordinates, and arclength-compatibility does not imply that.
The choice of isomorphism Γ_i ≅ (∂'X~)_i is non-canonical. The resulting surface depends on it, up to the twist parameter, which the note leaves implicit.
The decomposition claim in 6) (panachage = remove annulus + reglue cylinder) is only asserted in the R-analytic case. For general rectifiable Γ_i it would need welding arguments.

ideas.what: Cutting a Riemann surface along a rectifiable graph and regluing along boundary identifications
ideas.modern_name: conformal welding / cut-and-paste of Riemann surfaces

ideas.what: Shrinking/elongation of a collar annulus around boundary components (changing the modulus)
Mixed operation 'panachage': cutting off a region bounded by an arbitrary curve in a collar, as a composite of shrinking and elongations, with commutation across components
ideas.modern_name: Schiffer-type interior variation / local quasiconformal surgery near a curve

ideas.what: Use of these surgeries to build moduli of rigidified triples S ⊂ K ⊂ X (cellular maps / dessins with canonical conformal structure)
ideas.modern_name: moduli of ribbon graphs / dessins d'enfants; combinatorial Teichmüller theory
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartes and canonical conformal structures, but not this surgery calculus explicitly

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatic 'surgery calculus' of conformal surfaces: cut, reglue, shrink, elongate, mix, with commutation across components and an R-analytic normal form. It is evidently intended to define deformations and moduli of conformal dessins. He did not develop it into a theory in published form.
missed.quote: L'opération de panachage revient dans tous les cas à une composition de 1°) l'enlèvement R-analytique d'une couronne autour de C 2°) R-analytique Recollement par un cylindre les deux bords de la couronne enlevée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly subsumed by plumbing/grafting coordinates and conformal welding. The specific framing (rectifiable gluing data as the primitive, operations on a graph-decorated surface) is a mild historical curiosity rather than a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard cut-and-paste and collar-modulus surgery on Riemann surfaces, well known in Teichmüller theory. Its interest is biographical: it shows Grothendieck around 1984 working on analytic foundations for moduli of dessins. No new result is stated.
transcription_corrections: 'pancharge' should read 'panachage' (mixing): 'Opération mixte : panachage', 'commutation de l'opération de panachage', 'L'opération de panachage revient...'
'voisinage standard de chaque composante i du de ∂X~' should read '... de ∂'X~' (distinguished boundary, with prime)
Margin reads roughly 'C'est une composition rétrécissage ∘ élongation ... ou deux élongations' ('rétrécissage', not 'rétraction')

Item 6: 'Cas d'une composante C de K ... plongée R-analytique isolée' (the word read as 'bords' is probably 'courbe' or similar). The decomposition is numbered 1°) enlèvement R-analytique d'une couronne autour de C, 2°) R-analytique recollement...
Final lines likely read 'Relations avec les petits plongements conformes d'une petite couronne...' rather than 'recollement avec les petits plongements'
Second '4)' heading is a Grothendieck numbering slip (should follow 5).
